_about: World population, people by astronomers' year, for the People curve of the Time Machine bench (experiments/time-machine.html) and any timeline that wants it. Read from Our World in Data's long-run population series (which joins HYDE 3.3 before 1800, Gapminder to 1950 and the UN's World Population Prospects after) and thinned: every thousand years to year 0, every century to 1700, every decade to 1900, every five years after. Between points, interpolate linearly. HOW SURE: before 1800 these are reconstructions, not counts, and the HYDE authors give wide ranges; the deep past is uncertain by a factor of two or more. After 1950 the figures are censuses and registers and are good to a few percent. A curve drawn from this is a shape, and the number at any one year is 'about'.
source: Our World in Data, “Population – HYDE, Gapminder, UN – Long-run data” [dataset], fetched 30 Sep 2026 from ourworldindata.org/grapher/population (World). Underlying: PBL Netherlands Environmental Assessment Agency, HYDE 3.3 (2023); Gapminder, Population v7 (2022); United Nations, World Population Prospects (2024).

_range: from and to are the store years (astronomer's years) the curve is meaningful between — its first and last points; minPoints is the fewest points a period must hold for the curve to be offered (Prompt-Build-Timeline-Stack.md, part 6, 10 Oct 2026)
